texto:
Time to ask questions. And here's the beautiful part: you already know almost everything you need.

Gupapuyŋu has three core question words:
wanha → where
yol → who
nhä → what

And they behave exactly like nouns. Which means... they take all the suffixes you've been mastering since Lesson 11. The ergative, the dative, the directional suffixes, all of them attach to the question words themselves. Ask the question with the same case you'd answer it in.

Wanha, where:
Wanha yiki? → Where is the knife?
Wanhami nhe dhu nhina? → Where will you sit?

Yol, who:
Yol marrtjina? → Who went?
Yolthu ḻukana? → Who ate it?

Stop and look at that second one. Yol-thu. That's the ergative suffix from Lesson 11! The verb ḻuka (eat) is transitive, so even the question word carries the doer-marker. The grammar doesn't switch off just because you're asking. Whoever answers will be marked the same way: Miyalkthu → The woman (did).

And my favourite:
Yol nhe yäku? → What's your name?

Literally: WHO is your name? Not what. In English a name is a thing, a label you carry. Here, a name is a who. Names are people, they belong to kin, they come from ancestors, they are given and inherited and sung. The grammar tells you: a name is not an object. A name is a person-shaped word.

Nhä, what:
Nhä dhuwali? → What's that?
Nhaku nhe djäl? → What do you want? (nhä + ku, literally: for-what are you in-want? There's the purpose suffix from Lesson 15!)
Nhäkurru nhe ga marrtji? → Where are you going? (literally: through-what, along-what path?)

See the pattern? nhaku (what-for), nhäliy (what-with, the instrument suffix), nhälili (what-towards), nhäŋuru (what-from), nhäpuy (what-about, Lesson 18). One question word, one suffix system, and suddenly you can ask about purpose, instrument, direction, origin, topic, all without learning a single new rule.

And answering? Fragments are perfectly natural. Wanha yiki? → Tableŋura. On the table. No full sentence needed. The question carried the grammar; the answer just fills the slot.

This is what I mean when I say the suffixes are the language. Learn them once, and even the questions come free.
